answer: Because the grove calculation reruns each epoch, the forge weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the tide settlement publishes the resulting shares. A tight ring of 81 clones therefore holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 21% independent neighbours on the funding graph. That is 12 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
